newsitem.title: BELARUS: Ukraine says U.S. overreacts to drunk driving case.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says U.S. overreacts to drunk driving case.

text.p: Ukraine on Tuesday accused Washington of overreacting by publicly asking Kiev to waive diplomatic immunity for the wife of a Ukrainian diplomat charged with causing a car accident after drinking alcohol.

"A diplomat's wife got a bit tight and got behind the wheel. There are stories like that about foreign diplomats in Kiev every day, but we don't tell the whole world about it," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko said during a visit to neighbouring Belarus.
Udovenko, in Minsk to initial a border agreement between the two former Soviet republics, was responding to an announcement by U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns on Monday.

Burns said Olesy Yarotskiy, wife of second secretary Vadym Yarotskiy, would appear in court for prosecution if the Ukrainian government waived her immunity -- or her driving privileges would be suspended for a year.

Yarotskiy, 45, was charged with driving while intoxicated after she failed a breathalyser test following the collision late on Saturday. Her car struck a second car, pushing it into the car ahead of it. No one was injured.

It was the fourth drunken driving incident involving a diplomat from the former Soviet Union in the Washington area this year, and the third in recent months involving a Ukrainian living in North America.

Figure skating star Oksana Baiul was admitted to an alcohol education programme after crashing her car while under the influence of alcohol, and a Ukrainian diplomat in the Canadian city of Toronto was declared persona non grata after he was charged with drunk driving.
